transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t stop worrying about everything. My mind keeps jumping from whether this new partnership at the lab is going to cost me my position, to whether my data are wrong, bills piling up, my family thinking I’m falling behind… and whether I’ve already messed up my chances of getting into grad school.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying?

About seven months now. It really started around the time the lab’s funding changed and they brought in that commercial partnership—everything started being run differently, and I haven’t been able to stop worrying since.
When these worries start, do you find it difficult to control or stop them?

Yeah, it’s really hard to stop. I’ll try to focus on one thing, like finishing a report or checking an assay, but then one worry leads to another. Before I know it, I’m just staring at the screen, running through every possible way things could go wrong.
Have you noticed any physical muscle tension or tightness in your body along with this worry?

Yeah. My shoulders and neck are tight most of the day, and I catch myself clenching my jaw while I’m looking over spreadsheets. By evening I’ve usually got a headache and feel stiff, like I’ve been carrying equipment around all day.
Have you been having any trouble falling or staying asleep, or having restless, unsatisfying sleep?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my sleep specifically.
Do you often feel restless, keyed up, or on edge?

Yeah, especially at work. I feel wound up and can’t really settle into my chair—I’m tapping my foot, checking messages, or walking back to the instrument room for no real reason. Even normal lab noises can make me jump.
Have you been feeling easily fatigued or worn out more quickly than usual?

Yeah. Even if I’ve been in bed a full night, I wake up feeling like I pulled an all-nighter. By the time I’m labeling samples at work, or trying to make dinner for my family, I just feel heavy and mentally drained.
